purpose: Tests whether null-witness classes are idempotent: u^2 equiv_M u. Runs suffix_count=2 for comparison against Gate 1b suffix_count=1 data. If TV(response(u), response(u^2)) < eps_eq, the class is idempotent. A nontrivial idempotent (a^2=a with a!=0,1) would prove the monoid is not a group.

ASSERT.description: True invariance assertion — testing if A^2 = A

MISLEADING_ASSERT.description: Misleading assertion — testing if M^2 = M

BOUNDARY.description: Pure delimiter — testing if B^2 = B

predictions.H_idempotent_assert: ASSERT class: if K_a with a~0.38, then a^2~0.14. K_A^2 != K_A. Full response TV(u, u^2) should be measurably > 0. NOT idempotent on operator level.
predictions.H_idempotent_boundary: BOUNDARY class: if K_b with b~0.80, then b^2~0.64. K_B^2 != K_B. Also NOT idempotent.
predictions.H_idempotent_misleading: MISLEADING class: if K_m with m~1.55, then m^2~2.4. K_M^2 != K_M. NOT idempotent.
predictions.decisive_test: TV between suffix_count=1 (from Gate 1b) and suffix_count=2 (this experiment) distributions. If TV < 0.01 for any class, that class IS idempotent at the response-law level. If TV >> 0.01 for all classes, no idempotents exist. The ASSERT class at a~0.38 is the closest to a^2=a=0 (total absorption).
predictions.multiplicative_test: If K_a operator model holds: L(u^2)/L(u) should equal L(u)/L(baseline) = a_u. So L(u^2) = a_u^2 * L(baseline). Verify this prediction cellwise.

estimated_calls: 3 classes x 2 surfaces x 3 vars x 8 vals x 1 depth = 144 endpoints + 24 prefixes = 168 forwards, ~3 min CPU
